Part B: After mixing equal volumes, each concentration halves, so [Mg2+] = 1.0e-3 M and [OH-] = 5.0e-7 M. Q = 1.0e-3 × (5.0e-7)^2 = 2.5e-16. That is smaller than Ksp, so no precipitate forms.

Common ion OH- shifts the equilibrium Mg(OH)2 ⇌ Mg2+ + 2OH- to the left (Le Chatelier), so less solid dissolves
answers.final_answer: The solubility in (c), 1.4e-8 M, is much lower than in (a), 1.1e-4 M, because of the common-ion effect

Part A: Ksp = [Ag+]^2[CrO4^2-]. If s is the molar solubility, then 4s^3 = 1.1e-12, so s^3 = 2.75e-13 and s ≈ 6.5e-5 M.

Part B: Mixing equal volumes halves each concentration, so [Ag+] = 1.0e-3 M and [CrO4^2-] = 1.0e-7 M. Q = (1e-3)^2(1e-7) = 1e-13. This is less than Ksp, so no precipitate forms.

Part C: Here 4s^2... no — in this solution [CrO4^2-] ≈ 0.05 M and [Ag+] = 2s. So (2s)^2(0.05) = 1.1e-12, giving 4s^2 = 2.2e-11, s^2 = 5.5e-12 and s ≈ 2.3e-6 M.

answers.brief_reasoning: After 1:1 dilution: [Ag+]=1.0e-3 M, [CrO4^2-]=1.0e-7 M; Q=(1e-3)^2(1e-7)=1.0e-13, which is less than Ksp=1.1e-12
answers.final_answer: Q = 1.0×10^-13 < Ksp, so no precipitate forms

answers.brief_reasoning: Common-ion effect: the added CrO4^2- raises Q above Ksp, so by Le Chatelier's principle the dissolution equilibrium shifts left and less solid dissolves
answers.final_answer: Solubility in (c) is lower than in (a), about 2.3e-6 M vs 6.5e-5 M, because of the common-ion effect (equilibrium shifts toward the solid)

answers.brief_reasoning: Ksp is an equilibrium constant that depends only on temperature; adding the salt shifts the position of equilibrium, not the constant
answers.final_answer: Incorrect: Ksp stays the same at constant temperature; only the solubility changes
